text:
I bought a pre-built with a 1660s in 2019.  The 1660s was a beast of a single fan GPU but it eventually started dying on me.  I was limited in what i could get from my Power Supply Unit, as well as the size of my case (no 3-fan cards.  Some dual fan cards were also too big).  I got the 3060 to replace it quickly for $289.  Its a solid improvement, i can game at 1440p ultra at above 60FPS, and it works fantastic with Blender, Adobe suite, Davinci, and my other art software.  

This will tide me over fine for now.  I plan to build my own PC from in the future, when prices on the next get cards come down some.  This whole experience really made me realize, however, that Prebuilt PCs are often not very modular, because when something breaks or when you want to replace something, you often need to upgrade something else and spend even more money.  So next time im definitely building my own PC

text: Nvidia's gpu naming is wack but actually kinda ez to understand. simply going up from 10 series to 20 series doesn't mean ur gonna have better performance. if it ends in like 80 then its high end, if it ends in 60 its mid tier, and if it ends in 70 its a hybrid. so like a 1080 outperforms a 2060 in most cases. and then if theres a ti or a super that means its like a better version thats slightly more expensive (at msrp of course) and slightly better. then you have the gt vs gtx vs rtx. gt (as in gt 710 or gt 1030) is made for office work and extremely light (think minecraft) gaming. gtx is made for gaming (but without ray tracing) and then rtx is ray tracing and rather high end (also means that its near impossible to obtain one right now).

text:
@Christian Diaz... That's the 20 series, the 30 series 'RTX 3060' Is ampere. And the 10 series is Pascal. Difficult to compare consoles with PC lol

From my understanding the PS5 doesn't run native resolution over 1080p. Or proper MSAA anti-aliasing. But all 1440p - 4K (native resolution) PC benchmarks won't be compatible, You would need DLSS for comparison. Pretty sure all the consoles upscale

Also most dynamic reflections can be disabled on consoles, check out the Gaming Nexus comparison, Where in Dirt2 on PC reflections at even ultra low, Were Far better (as in Turned On lol) The PS5 cleverly uses increased contrast to trick the eye and add perceived depth to the lighting. But in dirt2 a PS5 is equivalent to a GTX 1060 'IF it had dlss' But in other games the consoles can performs much higher equivalent to a 3060 - 2070, It depends

But most midrange graphics cards can do native 1440p, When you balance dynamic shading and reflections, Even a GTX 1070 will run GTA5 with an ENB (RT graphics mod) Ultra at 'native 4K' 60+fps. Therefore most higher end cards, RTX 2070 up will do Native 4K with balanced graphics settings at 60+fps in almost all modern titles, leaving out DLSS on top

Hype is the problem for anything now. But Not even $3000 laptops can perform like desktops at half the cost. They would thermal throttle, Let alone a $500 console, But they're Great Value!

@Christian Diaz... If his PC is for gaming, Then it sounds like a bad combination. Because in gaming the graphics card is more important, and depending how high spec, Too much of the budget spent elsewhere, CPU, Ram, Case etc

A intel 4 core 3770k-6700k is more of a match for the 4gb GTX 1650, but that card is not really for demanding modern games, over 720-1080p (limited vram) Low-Medium textures (limited vram) and medium settings, lower draw distances. I'd say if your just a hobbyist go for the 3060 it'll be plenty, but if your rendering for a profession or looking at getting into a profession that requires rendering often then get the 3070 👍cost and availability are the biggest factors at the moment with the current GPU shortage though, so if you could possibly wait it out till 2022 you might get a better deal

author: @zk4929

text: @zk4929  I was also going to get the 3090 until it became the price of gold 😅 I'm waiting it out a couple years with a 3060 Ti then upgrading to the 3090 when prices fall. I wouldn't focus so much on the amount of memory that the 3060 has over the 3070 though because the 3070 operates with a higher memory interface. Think of the 3060 like a wide pipe with water passing slowly whereas the 3070 is a slimmer pipe but with water passing much quicker, so in reality there's not much of a different when looking at memory, I think the 3070s increased amount of cuda cores will be the biggest benefit in cutting down render times. In all honesty though you couldn't go wrong with either there both going to render fine it's just the time it takes will likely be quicker on the 3070. I'd keep asking about and get some other opinion's maybe call some computer store's and ask them what they'd recommend as I'm not a massive computer Wiz so best to get a few opinions before you pay out

text: The RTX 3060 purports to have 12gb of VRam but what they are not telling people is that it's almost entirely useless because it also has 192 bit bandwidth making it just a slight upgrade from your old, reliable 1060 that grants you unusable access to raytracing and other advanced features that won't work without a wider bandwidth. The 3060TI is a much better choice and if you can put an extra $100.00 or so down the true sweet spot of this generation of Nvidia cards is actually the 3070 line. The 3070 is the card that will carry you for years as a one time investment just like the 1060 did back in the day.

text: The 12Gb might be useful for cg artists to fit scene in the memory for rendering.
author: @zk4929

text: @zk4929  That's true but if that were the reason then they should be marketing it as a cheap workstation solution not a gaming card. My understanding is that they actually did it to drive up demand for the card over the much better 3060TI and 3070. Comparing it back to my current ASUS 1060 6GB , in that era, it would have been more like a 970. I can run Cyberpunk at descent settings without raytracing, yes the FPS is low by godly standards but it's more than playable between 30 and 60FPS and my card is a mini combined with an i5 CPU and a dollar store motherboard. I can't count on the 3060 to still be there 6 years from now running the latest stuff. It's a slight upgrade that would allow raytracing in Cyberpunk at the cost of many FPS but it also would mean a PSU upgrade so that's extra plus I'd have to worry about cooling and noise dampening so that's more extra. If artists can make use of this card then I think that's great but I don't think that was NVidia's goal. In fact they may raise the price if they find that artists are an unintended but hungry market.

text:
For gaming, the GTX 3060 has better price-to-performance ratio than the GTX 1060 6GB (by a quarter or a bit more), but is in a higher price bracket. It's more like a slightly-higher-end card of a newer generation than a true successor to the GTX 1060 6GB. That said, almost a successor? Yeah

Based on MSRP (not practical prices), the GTX 2060 was already a good successor (if slightly overpriced). In terms of practical prices, it was more just a higher-end model and a slight upgrade price-to-performance. Also, generation-over-generation, the RTX 3060 isn't much better than the RTX 2060 in raw gaming performance. In that sense, it's a failure.

That's also not counting the GTX 1060 3GB, which was the real value option and still has no successor. The GTX 1660 Ti was kind of, but just not that big an upgrade in raw performance. I do think that the RTX 3050 will blow all of the previous options out of the water, though.

Clearly, for productivity the 3060 is a big upgrade all-around, as well.

text:
3060 is a waste of money, a mockery by Nvidia

The MSRP for the 2060 at launch was set to 349 bucks, but after the release of Super variants, the MSRP was decreased to 299$.
So +10% of price, for around 20% better performance with this 3060.
Same tier performance of 2060 Super, same tier of price.
But, in the real world with scalped price, the cost will be higher even in comparison with 2070 Super, that is defenetely faster.
Further, while 3060 Ti have slightly better performance than 2080 Super (399 vs 699 MSRP), 3060 have slighlty better performance of the 2060 Super (329 vs 399), this after adopting new node and architecture.
Even the efficiency is nearly the same (170 vs 175 Watt of TDP).
Other datas: 3060 Ti, with 25% lower price than the 3070, have only 10% less the performance. 
3060 with 21% lower price than 3060 Ti, have 25% to 30% less the performance, so the performance/cost ratio is worse. If we consider that GA106 is way smaller than GA104, and that GA106-300 used for 3060 is a cut-down of the full chip (32 vs 28 SMs), they charging premium price on a lower-end product, that is simply ridicolous, a really shame.
Some quotes:

"Last gen flagship performance, for last gen mid range pricing, not last gen 5700 performance for f*ucking 5700 XT pricing two years later, nobody ask for this." - Moore's Law is Dead

"Nvidia at this point realized that their products do not have to be exciting. They just have to exist." - Gamer Nexus

​ @salehs3952  so you're comparing a product to an entire market? How is that anything but a non sequitur? 

Yes, 3060s are nearly $1000 right now (actually $800 - just checked the local scalper listings), because NO GPU is available right now at anything approaching MSRP. Everything is inflated, massively. Of course the 3060 is going to be inflated, because as shocking as this might be, the 3060 is, in fact, actually a subset of "everything". 1080TIs are running around $800 right now, for old, used cards, so $1000 for a brand new card that has DLSS and ray tracing would hardly be a bad deal at the moment, and their actual price of ~$800 is honestly pretty decent if you're actually desperate enough to buy a GPU right now.

If you don't like the 3060 that's fine. You're free to argue that point. But blaming it for an entire market that was wildly inflated before it even came along is rather silly.

text:
The idea that x60 is "mid-range" is strange to me. I always thought of the 70 series as the mid-range, which made sense back when they only costed about $320-380.

Also, people keep saying "X264-like", but to get similar performance from X264, it would require something like an overclocked 3950X or 5950X, maybe even a 3970X with SMT off. That's a lot of processing and power wasted, so I don't really think it's actually fair to call it X264-like (though, I get why that was said in the first place).

In my tests and from tests I've seen, Turing NVENC is generally better than X264 slow, especially when you use Xaymar's StreamFX. It's really in a class of it's own, especially when you consider the power usage and little to no impact is has on your system.

Edit: Also, there really needs to be a new CS:GO test. That standard test that everyone uses is incredibly not representative of the real gameplay. The test with a Zen 2 CPU and 2000 series GPU show the game averaging about 450 FPS at 1080p, but in reality, I get about 200-290 most times, even with many of the settings cranked down.

I ask myself the same thing as a consumer. The 3060 TI seems like the clearly superior product - in both bang-for-buck and raw performance.

I think the 12GB thing is mainly a response to AMD because it was a point of embarrassment for Nvidia, and something the community were immediately displeased with for Ampere. Does it make much sense to "fix" that problem after the fact only on your lower-tier cards? Not really... but what is logical to the consumer and what the exec's think looks good for the company are often two completely different things...

text:
Lol all the youtube idiots are out today. 

I dunno if you people realize, but there are no GPUs available right now and silicon shortages globally are real. Car companies already have to lower their production lines because there's no orders in for this year for the IC chips they use in cars. All of 2021's silicon stock has been spoken for. 

The reality is that titles like "Ti" and "Super" are used to explain the best of a batch of created GPUs. It's like picking the best fruit or the best cookies from a batch. In the past, there was enough stock that Nvidia stopped selling lower end parts because they can just be melted down and try again for a better batch. However, Nvidia is literally going to just sell any usable GPUs their factories can churn out and label them appropriately to their performance level. That's why 1070s are going back on sale because really bad batches end up coming out at the 1070 tier of quality.

text:
Relevant To Your Previous Video - Reacting To XQC's PC Build
A few small thing that could be explained about building a pc these days for newbies

ps. it would also be easier if these were segmented on Youtube so people could click each segment title if they already know some of them in a video.

In no particular order:

(a) Front panel connectors (Power switch/LED/Reset switch/Speaker/USB 3.0/USB-c) - where they go and what order they go in (it does show in manuals)
(b) Which way to plug cables into RGB header i.e cable arrow line up with the 5v/12v label on motherboard
(c) The removable bracket for fans/radiators where u install it outside of the case - not all cases have these but a good mention
(d) The rotation of fans in the case and which way is pull and push (i.e which way air flows through a fan when it is on)
(e) Motherboard stand-offs and m.2 stand-offs to make sure they are on etc
(f) Addressable RGB and normal RGB headers, interchangeable or not etc
(g) Pre-installed heatsinks for m.2 SSD and that they need to be removed
(h) The alignment of the screw holes when putting in a graphics card - (Lmao)
(i) Which power supply cables plug into which part of the motherboard/GPU/SSD/HDD
(j) Motherboard Lights or speaker beeps which show what issues there are with the pc
(k) Pre-mounted clips around the CPU for AMD motherboards and to check your cooler to see if you need them
(l) What some connectors on the motherboard are for i.e extra common features and stuff or just general ones
(m) Congratulations to Madison on the job, maybe have her do the video, so we can see another build by her, ROG Reboot was friggin great.
(n) Explain how motherboard hdmi doesnt work unless you have an APU or something?
(o) How to screw fans onto the radiator of an AIO
(p) GPU sag brackets
(q) Obvs dual channel RAM installation and which slots first
(r) How different/multiple slots in the case mean you can attach different size fans
(s) How much thermal paste to put on CPU
(t) Which slots on B550 are gen 4 like
(u) how to enable XMP or DCOP
(v) Just mention how Dust Filters can save a PC 
(w) How many intake vs outake fans is good/alright
(x) How the intel cpu cover comes off after installing the cpu and you shouldn't pull on it
(y) How we as viewers would like Madison to host the video
(z) show some cable tie tricks - then plug - then show good cable management

when I Upgrade I want something that has built in water cooling, so I don't need to void a warranty doing it myself. I want it to be more quite i'm also then going to upgrade my PSU thats 550w to something like a 1000 watt or 1500 watt PSU. why so over kill? Because I want the PSU to last a long time and give my self plenty of upgrade room in the future. plus for a while while i have a less powerful pc the new better PSU will not need to work as hard so it won't put out as much heat and thus the fan for it won't need to kick on as much.
But the only real upgrades I'm looking for right now is a large ssd or m.2 drive about 2tb if not more for the newer games that need a fast ssd to load maps right off the storage device. The second thing i'm going to get is the better PSU so i can start getting better parts for my pc.
i'm super lucky that my motherboard has like 6 sata ports and an m.2 slot i'm using 3 of my sata ports. a 128gb for a boot drive, a 2 tb for a important files drive and some games. and then my 4tb games drive that holds nothing but games.

text:
Don't ever buy a mining-rate-crippled graphics card.
Buy a 3070 or 3080 and mine your own crypto just a few hours each night to make up the price difference easily.

Every pickup truck is overpriced if you refuse to ever use its bed.  you will never outbid other shoppers who realize a pickup's value for both human and cargo transportation, if you only realize its value for human transportation. So if you buy a pickup, use the bed for a cargo-shipping side hustle, and the pickup will no longer be overpriced to you. The same goes with GPUs - full-time crypto miners need to make a long-term profit to justify buying the card at all, but you want to own it for gaming and can therefore justify buying it without making all of your money back by mining. Even a side hustle, the smaller amount of money gamers can make by casually mining part-time, would give them the power to dominate the new-GPU market and never perceive the existence of a shortage again.

The 3060 doesn't protect gamers. The 3060 and a lot of self-righteous talking tricks gamers into thinking that things are being done to protect them, while nothing is being done to protect the overall supply of graphics cards to gamers or make gamers more able to buy them.
3060 can't mine well -> full time crypto miners only buy 3070 and 3080 instead -> gamers who want the 3070 or 3080 can't find them and instead buy what they can, the 3060 -> same old horrendous shortages.
Nvidia didn't promise to weaken all cards for mining. Nvidia couldn't make this be about increasing production of all cards.

Nvidia now makes mining-only GPUs nearly identical to gaming GPUs, except with no value to gamers when resold (no more cheap used RTX **60s on eBay in perfect condition because their miners undervolted them in a chilled air-filtered shed for 2 years) and hopes everyone will also take it for granted that the un-gameable GPUs that will ruin that market aren't cut-down new gaming GPUs or eating into new gaming GPU production in the other most obvious way - being a giant wasteful diversion of development effort, funds, and semiconducting materials.

Trying to protect gaming GPU supply by starting mass production of nearly identical GPUs with tiny tweaks to make them incapable of gaming is like trying to save the environment by subsidizing coal. Nvidia's entire plan is stupid and dishonest, and limiting the 3060 is just part of it. Say NO to the 3060 and similar cards in the future.

text:
Half the arguments in this video made no sense. A Gtx 1060 in FS at ultra is 24 fps but the 3060 is 46. If you're locking to 30 which is more than enough for FS then the difference between 3060 and 1060 is just High vs Ultra preset (Ultra requires 50mbps down which most people on a 1060 probably won't have). It says in CS GO you want no less than double the framerate of your refresh rate but the 1060 handled 330fps, just under 3x the refresh rate of a 120hz monitor (likely the upper limit of refresh rates for 1060 owners). The 3060 IS a better card but this video seems to either test games which aren't very good at demonstrating that or the hoops which are being jumped through to showcase that point are making it all seem very uninformed. 

I mean, seriously, does anyone aim for 2x their refresh rate in games? And what CPU was that 3060 running with because 1060 users aren't sitting on a 5950x that's for sure. The upper possibility of the card might be much higher but all of the use cases in this video seem so out of touch with what the average 1060 user is going to be doing with it that it should not be recommending the card based on these findings at all.

text: You actually can just keep dropping the resolution if DLSS is supported.  If you turn on upscaling from 720 to 1080p there's basically no noticeable difference outside the performance gain.  The downside is the way DLSS works it's not going to be implemented on every title unless the engine comes with it included already.  One thing ATI has with FidelityFX is that it's much easier to implement in your projects.  So even if it's technically worse (ATI leads to aliasing whereas DLSS leads to artifacting from the testing I've done/seen) it's still easier to implement, so it wins in my book.  To be fair, I've had a lot more time playing with implementing FidelityFX than I have DLSS with the cards I had on loan.  I'm still using a Vega 64 and RX580 8 GB; did have a Vega 56 but scored a brand new 64 for ~340 bucks about a year ago.  I tossed the 56 on auction, and it ran up to 650.  Basically I got a free Vega 64 and then some, so I'm happy for now even if they are old cards.  I would like to get a 6800XT as an upgrade/for fidelityfx testing.  Eventually I'll get an Nvidia card for dlss testing too, but they're going to have to be at least MSRP used.

text:
So you still get at least 60fps at 1080p with a GTX 1060 with less power draw in most games with few exceptions. In this video Linus tells us, Nvidia targets people with a 1060 to upgrade. But looking at the Steam hardware survey more than 66% of all gamers use 1080p displays for gaming. Only about 13% use anything above...

Now maybe people are going for high refresh rates? But high refresh rates are only relevant for a limited amount of games. Also the tests they have made (referencing in the video) even state that it will mostly have an impact for professional players... which is also a minority.

But hey, you can get RTX with this 3060, right? Yeah, at 60 fps maybe... so Nvidia still devides their own audience because if you buy one of these you can choose between fine looking raytracing or a high refresh rate. So you probably have to decide upgrading your current monitor... try out raytracing first and notice that it's not as impressive as Nvidia stated at all. So maybe upgrade your monitor before thinking about a new GPU.

Anyway it's not that you would even be able to buy one without paying double the price or something. However this card definitely does not target people having a 1060 currently. If Nvidia would offer a really good deal here for everyone with a 1060, they would sell more 1060s instead of 1050 Tis. But they don't because they obviously know that everyone would get a 1060 being fine for years.

Heck 2014's Titan Z and any Titan after it had more VRAM than the RTX 3080 over six years later. Let that sink in, no matter if it's 60% cheaper and faster, we talking ages in PC tech.
So, the RTX 3080 is a compromise when it comes to its useful life and I guess Nvidia made it that way on purpose, not just to have a lower MSRP than the (Radeon) RX 6900 XT from AMD.
